rationale: Ground truth is sparse (an already-resolved 'move helpers to utils' comment plus an LGTM), so recall is similar and unremarkable for both. Both independently surface the same two strongest, diff-grounded findings — the identical unfixed TOCTOU race in diffusion_engine.py and the two regression tests that only assert fut.cancelled() and don't actually catch a crashed pump thread — lending them credibility. X presents these with tighter prioritization, concrete proposed code diffs, and one additional well-reasoned novel finding (the _completed_outputs leak on the non-racy abort ordering) plus a specific pytest-version verification of the weak-test claim. Y has a comparably strong unique finding (AMD CI failure correlated via pytestmark to the new tests) but its 'Validated' section repeats the same two claims (wrong test file name, 'all 3 fail' inaccuracy) three-plus times nearly verbatim, which is noisy and hurts actionability/precision by inflating apparent finding count without added value.
